blocks.content: 1. INTRODUCTION TO SUBJECT–VERB AGREEMENT

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Basic Rule: A singular subject requires a singular verb, and a plural subject requires a plural verb.
Subjects connected by 'or', 'nor', 'either...or', or 'neither...nor' make the verb agree with the nearest subject.
'A number of' takes a plural verb, whereas 'The number of' takes a singular verb.
Collective nouns take a singular verb when treated as a single unit, but a plural verb when individuals act separately.
Units of distance, time, money, and measurement take singular verbs when representing a unified quantity.

blocks.content:
Subject–Verb Agreement means that the verb must agree with its subject in number and person.

A singular subject takes a singular verb, while a plural subject takes a plural verb.



Incorrect agreement is one of the most commonly tested areas in SSC examinations, especially in Error Detection and Sentence Improvement questions.



Example:

• He plays cricket. (Correct)

• They play cricket. (Correct)



Golden Principle:

The verb is controlled by the subject — not by the words placed near it.
2. BASIC RULE

Singular Subject → Singular Verb

Plural Subject → Plural Verb



Examples:

• The boy runs fast.

• The boys run fast.



Remember:

Singular verbs usually end in “s” or “es” in the present tense, while plural verbs do not.
3. WHEN TWO SUBJECTS ARE JOINED BY ‘AND’

Rule:

When two subjects are joined by “and,” the verb is usually plural.



Example:

• Ram and Shyam are playing.



Exception:

If the two nouns refer to the same person or idea, use a singular verb.



Example:

• Bread and butter is my favorite breakfast.
4. SUBJECTS JOINED BY ‘OR’, ‘NOR’, ‘EITHER…OR’, ‘NEITHER…NOR’

Rule:

The verb agrees with the subject closest to it.



Example:

• Either the teacher or the students are responsible.

• Either the students or the teacher is responsible.
5. INDEFINITE PRONOUNS

Indefinite pronouns such as each, everyone, someone, anyone, nobody, etc. always take singular verbs.



Examples:

• Everyone is present.

• Each of the players is ready.



Common Error:

Incorrect: Everyone are happy.

Correct: Everyone is happy.
6. ‘EACH’ AND ‘EVERY’

When ‘each’ or ‘every’ is used before subjects joined by “and,” the verb remains singular.



Example:

• Each boy and each girl is participating.
7. COLLECTIVE NOUNS

Collective nouns (team, committee, jury, family, audience) usually take a singular verb when the group acts as one unit.



Example:

• The team is winning.



However, when members act individually, a plural verb may be used.



Example:

• The team are arguing among themselves.
8. PHRASES BETWEEN SUBJECT AND VERB

Words such as with, along with, together with, as well as, in addition to, etc., do NOT affect the verb.



The verb agrees with the main subject only.



Example:

• The captain, along with the players, is practicing.
9. ‘A NUMBER OF’ vs ‘THE NUMBER OF’

A number of → plural verb

Example: A number of students are absent.



The number of → singular verb

Example: The number of students is increasing.
CHAPTER 3 : SUBJECT–VERB AGREEMENT (DETAILED MASTER CHAPTER)
10. NOUNS THAT ARE ALWAYS SINGULAR

Some nouns appear plural but are treated as singular.



Examples:

news, mathematics, physics, economics, furniture, advice, information.



Example:

• Mathematics is difficult.
11. NOUNS THAT ARE ALWAYS PLURAL

Certain nouns are always treated as plural.



Examples:

scissors, trousers, spectacles, clothes, police.



Example:

• The police are investigating the case.
12. TITLES AND NAMES

Titles of books, movies, organizations, and countries are treated as singular even if they look plural.



Example:

• “The United States” is a powerful country.
13. DISTANCE, TIME, MONEY, AND MEASUREMENT

When expressing a single amount or quantity, use a singular verb.



Example:

• Ten kilometers is a long distance.

• Five hundred rupees is too much.
14. ‘ONE OF THE’ RULE

rows: Refers to an indefinite plural quantity
Refers to a specific singular count or unit
Verb agrees with the closest subject noun
Group acts as a single cohesive entity
Members act individually or express disagreement

blocks.content:
After “one of the,” use a plural noun but a singular verb.



Example:

• One of the students is absent.
15. ‘MORE THAN ONE’

“More than one” takes a singular verb.



Example:

• More than one person has complained.
16. ‘A LOT OF’, ‘PLENTY OF’, ‘HALF OF’

The verb depends on the noun that follows.



Example:

• A lot of water is wasted.

• A lot of people are waiting.
17. GERUNDS AS SUBJECTS

When a verb acts as a noun (V-ing), it takes a singular verb.



Example:

• Swimming is good exercise.
18. INFINITIVES AS SUBJECTS

An infinitive phrase also takes a singular verb.



Example:

• To err is human.
19. RELATIVE PRONOUN ‘WHO’, ‘WHICH’, ‘THAT’

The verb agrees with the noun before the relative pronoun.



Example:

• She is one of the students who work hard.

• She is the only one who works hard.
20. THERE / HERE STRUCTURES

In sentences starting with “there” or “here,” the verb agrees with the real subject that follows.



Example:

• There are many books on the table.

• There is a book on the table.

items: SSC Exam Trap: 'A number of' is followed by a plural verb, but 'The number of' requires a singular verb.
Intervening phrases like 'as well as', 'along with', and 'together with' do not alter the main subject's agreement with the verb.
In relative pronoun clauses ('who', 'which', 'that'), the verb agrees with the antecedent noun preceding the pronoun.

blocks.content: 21. IMPORTANT SSC TRAPS

Incorrect: The list of items are on the desk.

Correct: The list of items is on the desk.



Incorrect: Each of the boys have completed the task.

Correct: Each of the boys has completed the task.



Incorrect: Bread and butter are my breakfast.

Correct: Bread and butter is my breakfast.
22. QUICK MEMORY RULES

1. Ignore words between subject and verb.

2. Indefinite pronouns are singular.

3. ‘And’ usually makes the subject plural.

4. ‘Or/Nor’ follow the nearest subject rule.

5. Collective nouns are usually singular.
23. PRACTICE QUESTIONS (SSC LEVEL)

Error Detection:



1. Each of the students have submitted the form.

2. The bouquet of flowers smell good.

3. Either the manager or the employees is responsible.



Fill in the blanks:



1. Everyone ______ ready for the trip. (is/are)

2. A number of players ______ injured. (was/were)

3. The quality of the apples ______ excellent. (is/are)



Answers:

1. has

2. smells

3. are responsible

Fill blanks → is, were, is.
24. CHAPTER SUMMARY

Subject–Verb Agreement ensures grammatical accuracy in sentences.



Key Takeaways:

• Singular subject → singular verb.

• Plural subject → plural verb.

• Ignore interrupting phrases.

• Follow proximity rule with ‘or/nor’.

• Indefinite pronouns are singular.



Mastering these rules will significantly improve accuracy in SSC grammar questions.
